question: Why did Isaiah Berlin warn that freedom understood as self-mastery could be used to justify coercion?
answer: Because it splits a person into a true, rational self and an unruly everyday one. Whoever claims to know the true self can coerce the actual one in its name. Berlin's 1958 lecture traced this to Rousseau's idea that a citizen may be forced to be free. For your own good is the opening line.
move: Distrust anyone who claims to know your real wishes better than you.
ask: When I push someone for their own good, am I respecting what they actually want?
reference: Berlin, Two Concepts of Liberty, in Four Essays on Liberty, Oxford University Press, 1969
